sentences.text: This pterosaur possessed robust and elongated wings that spanned approximately 1.2 meters across.
Its wing finger retained the standard four phalanges, distinguishing it from the related genus Beipiaopterus which lost the fourth one.
The leg bones show a specialized structure where the femur measures 6 cm in length while the tibia measures 96 mm, and the fibula is strongly reduced in size.
The foot claws were slightly curved, with the fifth toe reduced to a single claw.
Eighteen detached belly ribs were found preserved within the fossil matrix.
Most of the vertebrae in the fossil are severely damaged, making it impossible to determine their exact number.
The genus Eosipterus was named in 1997 by paleontologists Ji Shu'an and Ji Qiang, with the type species designated as Eosipterus yangi.
The genus name combines Greek words for 'dawn' and 'wing' with a Latin ending, though a grammar error resulted in the spelling 'Eosipterus' instead of the expected 'Eopterus'.
The specific name 'yangi' honors the paleontologist Yang Daihuan.
Eosipterus was the first pterosaur discovered in the western Liaoning region.
A 2006 cladistic study identified Eosipterus as a member of the family Ctenochasmatidae, with David Unwin further assigning it to the subfamily Ctenochasmatinae.
Fossil remains of Eosipterus date back to the Aptian stage, approximately 125 million years ago.
The time range for Eosipterus is from the Barremian to the Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
